name: Diabetes
shortDescription: Known as Madhumeha in Ayurveda, managing blood glucose through Kapha and Pitta dosha balancing.
causes: Excessive intake of sweets and heavy foods
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Madhumeha, it is a metabolic disorder (Prameha) dominated by Kapha dosha, which affects fat tissues and urine chemistry due to low digestive fire (Agni).

recoveryTimeline.description: Assess metabolic fire (Agni) levels
Deep cleansing herbs to remove blockages
Herbal supplements and diet charts
Adopting custom lifestyle schedules

faq.question: Is Ayurvedic treatment safe alongside insulin?
faq.answer: Yes, Ayurvedic herbs work synergistically and help reduce insulin resistance under professional Vaidya guidance.

name: PCOS
shortDescription: Hormonal and reproductive system restoration through ovarian tissue nourishment.
ayurvedicPerspective: Originates from a Kapha-Vata blockage in the channels regulating the reproductive fluids (Artava Srotas), resulting in cyst accumulation and metabolic stagnation.

recoveryTimeline.description: Clearing blockages in reproductive paths
Balancing Vata energy flow (Apana Vayu)
Nourishing ovaries and balancing insulin levels

faq.question: Can PCOS be completely cured by Ayurveda?
faq.answer: Yes, by targeting the root metabolic blockages, normal ovarian function and regular cycles can be restored permanently.

name: Arthritis
shortDescription: Addressing joint pain (Amavata or Sandhivata) by removing toxins and lubricating connective tissues.
causes: Exposure to cold and damp conditions
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Amavata (similar to Rheumatoid Arthritis) or Sandhivata (Osteoarthritis). It involves the accumulation of Ama (undigested toxins) in joint junctions due to impaired Agni.
lifestyleRecommendations: Daily application of warm sesame oil

recoveryTimeline.description: Consuming hot spices to clear raw metabolic toxins
Warm oil pooling and herbal lubrication
Strengthening bones and joints (Asthi Dhatu)

faq.question: How does Shallaki help with pain?
faq.answer: Shallaki is a natural anti-inflammatory agent that blocks inflammatory compounds without causing stomach irritation.

name: Migraine
shortDescription: Alleviating deep vascular headaches by soothing aggravated Pitta-Vata channels near the nervous system.
causes: Excessive heat and direct sun exposure
ayurvedicPerspective: Considered as Ardhavabhedaka, it is primarily a Vata-Pitta disorder aggravated by sluggish digestion (Mandagni), leading to heat blockages in head channels.

recoveryTimeline.description: Nasal drops (Nasya) to clear sinus and head channels
Shirodhara to relieve stress and lower vascular pressure
Digestive supplements to prevent toxic gas generation

faq.question: Why is Shirodhara recommended for migraines?
faq.answer: Shirodhara relaxes the central nervous system, reduces adrenaline levels, and dilates cranial vessels, preventing migraine triggers.

name: Psoriasis
shortDescription: Clearing systemic skin scaling and inflammation (Kitibha Kushtha) through blood purification therapies.
ayurvedicPerspective: Referred to as Kitibha Kushtha, it involves the accumulation of toxins in the skin tissues (Tvach), blood (Rakta), and lymphatic fluids (Lasika) due to incompatible food pairings.
lifestyleRecommendations: Applying cold-pressed coconut oil mixed with camphor

recoveryTimeline.description: Clinical Panchakarma to expel blood impurities
Bitter herb regimens to neutralize metabolic acid
Moisturising pastes and tissue building herbs

faq.question: What is Viruddha Ahara?
faq.answer: It refers to incompatible food combinations, like eating fish and milk together, which Ayurveda warns creates toxic blood reactions.

name: Obesity
shortDescription: Reversing lipid tissue overgrowth (Sthoulya) by accelerating metabolic fire (Agni) and modifying diet.
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Medoroga or Sthoulya. The fat tissue channel (Meda Vaha Srotas) becomes blocked, converting all nutrition into fat instead of building bone or muscle.
dietRecommendations: Warm honey water on empty stomach

recoveryTimeline.description: Dry powder massages (Udvartana) to break down fat
Herbs to accelerate liver fire (Dhatvagni)
Building muscle tissue while trimming lipids

faq.question: Why is cold water restricted in weight management?
faq.answer: Cold water dampens the digestive fire (Agni), slows down the metabolism, and increases Kapha dosha, which promotes fat storage.

name: Asthma
shortDescription: Relieving breath channel blockages (Prana Vaha Srotas) by clearing chest mucus.
causes: Exposure to cold air and dust
ayurvedicPerspective: Called Tamaka Shwasa. It originates in the digestive system, where impaired stomach digestion produces mucus that travels upwards and block breathing paths (Prana Vaha Srotas).
lifestyleRecommendations: Daily chest inhalation of steam with eucalyptus

recoveryTimeline.description: Applying salt-oil to chest with local heat
Expelling deep thoracic toxins via Vamana or herbs
Respiratory tonics (Rasayana) to strengthen airways

faq.question: Is Asthma treatment linkable to digestion?
faq.answer: Yes! Ayurveda teaches that weak stomach Agni creates toxic phlegm, which travels and constricts breathing channels.

name: Gastritis
shortDescription: Cooling burning sensations in the stomach (Amlapitta) by regulating digestive acid.
ayurvedicPerspective: Referred to as Amlapitta. Aggravated Pitta dosha increases the sourness and acidity of digestive fluids, leading to localized inflammation in stomach linings.

recoveryTimeline.description: Cooling sweet herbs to soothe inflamed lining
Mild purgation to throw out sour bile from the system
Restoring balanced digestive fire without generating acid

faq.question: How does Licorice help Gastritis?
faq.answer: Licorice root coats and protects the stomach lining, encouraging healthy mucus secretion to buffer against excess acid.

name: Insomnia
shortDescription: Calming hyperactive mind channels (Anidra) using soothing oil massages and mental adaptogens.
symptoms: Waking up in the middle of night
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Anidra. Caused by Vata-Tarpaka dryness. High Vata energy excites the mind, preventing the heavy, calming Kapha energy required to fall asleep naturally.
treatments: Pada Abhyanga (warm foot rub before bed)
lifestyleRecommendations: Massaging soles and temples with warm sesame oil

recoveryTimeline.description: Warm head oil drippings (Shirodhara) to quiet thoughts
Calming herbs to balance nervous transmission
Consistency in bedtime routines and nourishing diet

faq.question: Why buffalo milk for sleep?
faq.answer: Ayurveda considers buffalo milk heavier and more calming (inducing natural sleepiness) compared to cow milk.

name: Anxiety
shortDescription: Balancing neurological wind (Manovaha Srotas) through stabilizing breathing and brain tonics.
ayurvedicPerspective: A Vata disorder affecting the mind channels (Manovaha Srotas). The erratic nature of Vata mimics wind, causing racing thoughts, nervousness, and lack of grounding.

recoveryTimeline.description: Nourishing oil massage to lower erratic wind energy
Nootropic herbs to repair and soothe nervous tissues
Rigid sleep, eating, and meditation time mappings

faq.question: How does Ashwagandha calm anxiety?
faq.answer: Ashwagandha acts as an adaptogen that lowers cortisol levels, strengthens the nervous system, and calms Vata dosha.

name: Indigestion
shortDescription: Impairment of digestive capacity leading to gas, bloating, and abdominal discomfort.
ayurvedicPerspective: Caused by weak Agni (digestive fire) which fails to digest food properly, producing Ama (undigested toxic waste) that sits in the gut.

recoveryTimeline.description: Taking ginger and rock salt before meals
Fasting or light diet to digest raw toxins

faq.question: Can I drink water during meals?
faq.answer: Sipping small amounts of warm water during meals is beneficial, but drinking cold water or large quantities will extinguish Agni.

name: Diarrhea
shortDescription: Frequent loose watery stools caused by aggravated Apana Vata and high liquid intake.
ayurvedicPerspective: Aggravated doshas enter the digestive tract, impair Agni, and liquefy the fecal matter, pushing it downwards rapidly.

recoveryTimeline.description: Consuming astringent herbs like Bael
Gradually introducing thin rice gruel (Manda)

faq.question: Why is milk avoided in diarrhea?
faq.answer: Milk is heavy to digest and Kapha-promoting, which dampens the weak Agni further during diarrhea.

name: Constipation
shortDescription: Difficulty passing stools due to dryness in the colon from aggravated Vata dosha.
ayurvedicPerspective: Aggravated Apana Vayu dries up fecal matter in the large intestine, causing blockages in the colon channel.
dietRecommendations: Warm milk with ghee at bedtime

recoveryTimeline.description: Daily intake of warm ghee or castor oil
Regular Triphala intake at night

faq.question: Is Triphala habit-forming?
faq.answer: No, Triphala is a mild bowel tonic and rejuvenator, not a harsh stimulant laxative.

name: Thyroid / Goiter
shortDescription: Imbalance of Kapha-Vata affecting the neck channels and sluggish metabolism.
ayurvedicPerspective: Related to Galaganda or thyroid dysfunction, caused by vitiation of Kapha dosha affecting the medas (fat tissues) and throat channels.

recoveryTimeline.description: Clearing throat channels with Nasya and Guggulu
Nervous adaptogens like Ashwagandha

faq.question: How does Kanchnar Guggulu help?
faq.answer: It has scraping (Lekhana) properties that help clear lymphatic blockages and reduce glandular swellings in the neck.

name: Common Cold
shortDescription: Congestion and discharge of nasal channels from aggravated Kapha-Vata.
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Pratishyaya, caused by digestion impairment producing toxins that mix with Kapha and block nasal passages.

recoveryTimeline.description: Taking hot spices and steam
Applying Anu Taila nasal drops

faq.question: Can I take curd when I have a cold?
faq.answer: No, curd is highly mucus-forming (Abhishyandi) and will worsen congestion.

name: Sinusitis
shortDescription: Chronic sinus inflammation and pressure due to Kapha blockages in head cavities.
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Pinasa or Dustha Pratishyaya, it is a chronic Vata-Kapha condition where mucus hardens in the head channels.

recoveryTimeline.description: Hot steam with eucalyptus and hot spices
Nasya drops to purge head mucus

faq.question: Is Neti pot safe?
faq.answer: Yes, when performed with sterile lukewarm saline water and dried properly, it is excellent for nasal hygiene.

name: Anemia
shortDescription: Deficiency of red blood cells leading to paleness and low energy levels.
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Pandu Roga, caused by Pitta dosha impairing the blood tissue (Rakta Dhatu) formation and quality.
treatments: Mridu Virechana (mild laxative to clear Pitta)

recoveryTimeline.description: Mild liver detox to remove bile blockages
Iron and vitamin rich herb supplements

faq.question: Are Ayurvedic iron preparations safe?
faq.answer: Yes, classical Loha Bhasma is highly purified and processed with herbs to prevent constipation and ensure high absorption.

name: Jaundice
shortDescription: Liver dysfunction causing bile accumulation and yellowing of eyes/skin.
causes: Highly spicy, sour, and hot foods
ayurvedicPerspective: Referred to as Kamala, a severe Pitta condition affecting the liver (Yakrit) and blood tissues.
lifestyleRecommendations: Avoiding direct sunlight or hot environments

recoveryTimeline.description: Purgatives like Trivrit to flush excess Pitta
Consuming Bhumyamalaki and sugar water

faq.question: Is sugarcane juice good for Jaundice?
faq.answer: Yes, it provides instant glucose for liver cells and acts as a mild diuretic to flush out excess bilirubin.

name: Gout
shortDescription: Severe joint pain and inflammation from uric acid buildup due to blood-wind imbalance.
ayurvedicPerspective: Known as Vatarakta, where aggravated Vata dosha blocks the channels, causing blood (Rakta) to pool and inflame the joints.

recoveryTimeline.description: Blood purification herbs and cooling oils
Enema therapies (Basti) to regulate Vata

faq.question: Why is Giloy (Guduchi) highly praised for Gout?
faq.answer: Guduchi is a potent uric-acid modulator and blood purifier that balances both Vata and Pitta doshas.

name: Paralysis
shortDescription: Loss of motor function on one side of the body due to severe Vata blockage in brain channels.
ayurvedicPerspective: Called Pakshaghata, caused by severely aggravated Vata drying up the motor nerves and blood vessels of the brain.
dietRecommendations: Rich sesame oil & ghee cooked dishes

recoveryTimeline.description: Daily warm medicated oil massages and steam
Nerve regenerating herbs and enemas

faq.question: Can Ayurveda help after a stroke?
faq.answer: Yes, early Ayurvedic intervention (within 3 months of stroke) shows high success in regaining motor function and speech.

name: Parkinson's
shortDescription: Neurological tremors and stiffness caused by Vata dryness in brain cells.
ayurvedicPerspective: Referred to as Kampavata (trembling wind), a neurological condition where Vata dries up the brain cells and nerve roots controlling movement.

recoveryTimeline.description: Consuming Kapikachhu (natural L-Dopa source)
Shirodhara and enemas to hydrate tissues

faq.question: How does Kapikachhu work?
faq.answer: Kapikachhu contains high concentrations of L-Dopa, the direct precursor to dopamine, which restores normal transmission.

name: Epilepsy
shortDescription: Neurological seizure episodes caused by temporary blockages in memory and mental channels.
ayurvedicPerspective: Referred to as Apasmara, caused by Dosha accumulation blocking the memory channels (Manovaha Srotas), resulting in a sudden blackout of consciousness.

recoveryTimeline.description: Purging digestive toxins and applying head oils
Daily intake of medicated ghee and nervine tonics

faq.question: Why is old Ghee recommended for Epilepsy?
faq.answer: Old cow's Ghee has unique fat-soluble molecules that can cross the blood-brain barrier and nourish damaged brain cells.

name: Depression
shortDescription: Persistent sadness and low energy caused by sluggishness in mental channels (Tamas energy dominance).
ayurvedicPerspective: Called Avasada, caused by Tamas (darkness/dullness) blocking the heart-brain channels, weakening Prana Vayu and Sadhaka Pitta (courage fire).

recoveryTimeline.description: Pranayama and uplifting adaptogens like Saffron
Shirodhara and regular counseling therapy

faq.question: Does Ayurveda recommend counseling?
faq.answer: Yes, it is called Satvajaya Chikitsa (mental control therapy), focusing on shifting thoughts from Tamas (dullness) to Sattva (clarity).
